children.name: Pennaria
children.description: Pennaria — a genus of pennariidae in the family Pennariidae.

children.name: Pennaria disticha
children.description: Pennaria disticha, also known as the Christmas tree hydroid, is a species of athecate hydroid in the family Pennariidae.

children.name: Pennaria wilsoni
children.description: (from live material). Mature colonies comprising one to many branched stems to 20 cm long arising from a ramified hydrorhiza, stolons tubular, almost smooth in young colonies to rugose and gnarled in older colonies. Stems erect, monosiphonic, flexuous, cylindrical, perisarc smooth and shining, straight to weakly sympodial, a slight change of direction at origin of each primary branch; branches widely separated along stem in indefinite whorls of three, directed upwards at 30 − 40 º to stem. Stem widest at base, narrowing slightly distally, ringed above base with up to 50 deep annulations and with up to 20 deep annulations above origin of older branches; sometimes groups of annulations along stem not associated with branching. Hydranth pedicels variable in length (depending on age of colony), widely separated, given off more or less triserially, up to 15 on weakly annulated pedicels, sometimes with a smooth mid-section, branch always with a terminal hydranth. Hydranth long, cylindrical to spindle-shaped, hypostome flattened dome-shaped. Four to five, rarely six short capitate oral tentacles clustered around hypostome, tentacles transversely segmented, each segment with a small central reddish spot, capitala with batteries of nematocysts. Aboral tentacles long, slender, semicapitate, in one whorl of 7 - 8, arched in life, a thick fringe of nematocysts along the outer side of tentacle, inner side transversely segmented with large transparent cells with reddish inclusions.
